description: A comprehensive study of electronic circuits operating with continuous variable signals, encompassing diodes, transistors, amplifiers, operational amplifiers, and oscillators.

sections.title: Diode Circuits and Applications
sections.description: Analysis of PN junction diodes, Zener diodes, and their applications in rectification, clipping, and clamping.

key_concepts.explanation: Clippers are wave-shaping circuits that remove a portion of the input signal without distorting the remaining part. Clampers add a DC level to an AC signal, shifting the entire waveform up or down without changing its peak-to-peak shape.

Operates strictly in the reverse breakdown region. It maintains a constant output voltage across the load despite variations in input voltage or load current, provided the current remains between I_z(min) and I_z(max).

sections.title: BJT Biasing and Operating Regions
sections.description: Understanding the DC operation of Bipolar Junction Transistors, biasing techniques, and thermal stability.

key_concepts.explanation: A self-destructive process where an increase in temperature causes an increase in reverse saturation current, leading to higher collector current, increased power dissipation, and further temperature rise. Prevented by proper biasing (like Voltage Divider Bias).

results: Active Region: E-B junction forward biased, C-B junction reverse biased (Used for linear amplification).
Saturation Region: Both E-B and C-B junctions forward biased (Acts as a closed switch in digital circuits).
Cut-off Region: Both E-B and C-B junctions reverse biased (Acts as an open switch in digital circuits).

sections.title: Small Signal Amplifiers
sections.description: Low-frequency AC analysis of BJT and FET amplifiers using hybrid (h) and re models to determine gain and impedance.

results: Common Emitter (CE): High voltage and current gain, moderate input/output impedance, 180-degree phase shift. Best for general-purpose amplification.
Common Collector (CC / Emitter Follower): Voltage gain approx 1, high current gain, very high input impedance, low output impedance. Used heavily for impedance matching.
Common Base (CB): High voltage gain, current gain approx 1, very low input impedance, high output impedance. Used primarily for high-frequency applications.

sections.title: Operational Amplifiers (Op-Amps)
sections.description: Characteristics of ideal and practical Op-Amps and their implementation in linear and non-linear mathematical operations.

equations: Common Mode Rejection Ratio (CMRR): CMRR = 20 * log10(|Ad / Ac|) dB

key_concepts.explanation: In a closed-loop ideal op-amp with negative feedback, the differential input voltage is zero. Thus, the voltage at the inverting terminal is mathematically forced to equal the voltage at the non-inverting terminal.
The maximum rate of change of the output voltage per unit time. It dictates and limits the high-frequency operation of the op-amp for large signals. SR = 2 * pi * f_max * V_peak.

sections.title: Feedback Amplifiers and Oscillators
sections.description: Effects of negative feedback on amplifier parameters and the principles of positive feedback for generating oscillations.

key_concepts.explanation: For sustained, undamped oscillations, the total phase shift around the closed loop must be 0 or 360 degrees, and the magnitude of the loop gain (|A * beta|) must be exactly equal to 1.

results: Voltage-Series (Series-Shunt): Increases Input Impedance, Decreases Output Impedance.
Voltage-Shunt (Shunt-Shunt): Decreases Input Impedance, Decreases Output Impedance.
Current-Series (Series-Series): Increases Input Impedance, Increases Output Impedance.
Current-Shunt (Shunt-Series): Decreases Input Impedance, Increases Output Impedance.
